key_insight: Detonation-sprayed Fe-based amorphous coatings form dense fine-lamellar microstructures when droplets spread well, and this improves long-term corrosion and wear performance.
engineering_relevance: Optimizing spraying parameters and humidity exposure can help extend the service life of Fe-based protective coatings on carbon steel.
method: Fe-based amorphous coatings deposited on Q235 carbon steel by detonation spray
Spraying parameters varied to tune droplet spreading, porosity, and microstructure
Corrosion and tribological behavior tested under different humidity conditions
evidence_signal: The abstract reports disk-like droplets with high circularity/expansion factor, lower porosity linked to better corrosion resistance, and decreasing friction coefficient and wear rate as humidity increases.
watch_item: Results depend strongly on deposition quality; increased porosity or poorly optimized spray parameters can reduce long-term corrosion resistance.
paper_title: Long-term corrosion behaviors and wear behavior of Fe-based amorphous coatings in different humidity environments
